name: yaml-linepos-shape-change-speccy
behavioral_change: yaml v2.0.0 changed the shape of the `linePos` property on errors thrown by `parse`. In v_old (1.6.0) it was an object `{ start: { line, col }, end: { line, col } }`; in v_new (2.9.0) it is a tuple `[{ line, col }, { line, col }]` matching the new `error.pos`, and the `start` and `end` properties no longer exist.
downstream_effect: The downstream project's `loadSpec` catch block in lib/loader.js:183 reads `err.linePos.start.line`, which now throws a TypeError that escapes the catch block and replaces the intended `ReadError`. The two jest failures report only "Expected constructor: ReadError, Received constructor: TypeError" with frames in test/lib/loader.test.js; node_modules/yaml, the version numbers and linePos never appear, although the test title "Loader › loadSpec()" points toward lib/loader.js.
reference_fix: The reference fix edits the catch block in lib/loader.js so that it takes `err.linePos[0]` when `linePos` is an array, falls back to `err.linePos.start` otherwise, and omits the position prefix when neither is available.
documented_in: The yaml release notes for v2.0.0-5 (https://github.com/eemeli/yaml/releases/tag/v2.0.0-5), BREAKING CHANGES entry "Replace `error.offset` with `error.pos: [number, number]` (#260)", state that `error.linePos` is changed to a matching tuple of `{ line, col }` values, and the v2.0.0 release notes (https://github.com/eemeli/yaml/releases/tag/v2.0.0) link back to it; the entry is prose only with no code showing how to read the new shape.
failing_tests: test/lib/loader.test.js :: Loader › loadSpec() › errors when duplicate keys exist
test/lib/loader.test.js :: Loader › loadSpec() › throws ReadError for invalid YAML/JSON
